veranderings.voor: Soutwater bevat baie sout en ons vind
veranderings.na: Soutwater bevat baie sout, en ons vind
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb (Soutwater bevat / ons vind) take a comma before en.

veranderings.voor: Daar is wel 'n bietjie sout in, maar te min om sout te proe.
veranderings.na: Daar is wel 'n bietjie sout daarin, maar te min om dit te proe.
veranderings.rede: The stranded 'in' is spoken style and repeating 'sout' is wooden; 'daarin' and 'dit' read more naturally with the same meaning.

veranderings.na: vleilande. Daar is ook varswater in ys
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017 puts no comma before en in a list, and without it the long list of places runs on; a new sentence keeps every place and leaves the protected wording intact.

veranderings.voor: lê in die oseane en daardie water is sout
veranderings.na: lê in die oseane, en daardie water is sout
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb take a comma before en.

veranderings.voor: Die son maak die water warm en van die water
veranderings.na: Die son maak die water warm, en van die water
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb (Die son maak / van die water verander) take a comma before en.
The separable verb opstyg puts its particle at the end of the clause in natural Afrikaans; 'styg op in die lug' follows English word order.
'dit' points back to the waterdamp of the previous sentence, so the sentence reads as if water vapour is called evaporation; naming the change (from 'verander in waterdamp') fixes the reference.

veranderings.voor: seewater warm en van daardie water
veranderings.na: seewater warm, en van daardie water
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: two clauses each with their own subject and verb (Die son maak / van daardie water verdamp) take a comma before en.

veranderings.voor: en bly agter in die see
veranderings.na: en bly in die see agter
veranderings.rede: The separable verb agterbly puts its particle at the end of the clause in natural Afrikaans.

veranderings.voor: Na 'n ruk is die water weg en lê daar
veranderings.na: Na 'n ruk is die water weg, en lê daar
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: each clause has its own subject and verb (die water is / 'n wit lagie lê); the reviewer may judge the shared opening 'Na 'n ruk' makes it one sentence and drop this.

veranderings.voor: Water met baie sout in, soos
veranderings.na: Water wat baie sout bevat, soos
veranderings.rede: The stranded 'in' is spoken style; 'wat baie sout bevat' is standard written Afrikaans and matches the varswater entry beside it.

vlae.teks: Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en die see.
vlae.rede: The protected wording is 'Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en plante', but the lesson ends the list with 'die see' and has no 'plante'. The protected sentence does not occur in the lesson, so either the lesson or the protected entry is out of date; this is content, so it was not changed.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: Water verdamp ook uit riviere, damme, nat grond en plante
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: This protected wording does not appear in the lesson as written (the lesson has 'nat grond en die see'), so it protects nothing here; a person should check which version is intended.
